focus: Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System, Section 11 (Calculations). Explain the probability that an attacker with a share q of the hash power ever catches up from z blocks behind. Let the learner change q and z and see the catch-up probability and the Poisson-weighted sum used in the paper. Show how the probability drops as z grows. Check that the probability is 1 when q >= p, and that for q = 0.1 and z = 5 the result is about 0.0009137 as in the paper's table.
audience: Computer engineering undergraduates who know basic probability but not cryptocurrencies
